verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच तं मुनिं जनमेजयः । गर्ह्यं भवान् गर्हयते निन्द्यं निन्दति मां पुनः ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Having got this high boon from the great God, the son of Satyavati, was one day engaged in rubbing his sticks for making a fire.

verses.sanskrit: धिक्कार्यं मां धिक्कुरुते तस्मात्त्वाऽहं प्रसादये । सर्वं हीदं दुष्कृतं मे ज्वलाम्यग्नाविवाहितः ॥२॥
verses.english: While thus engaged, the illustrious Rishi, O king, saw the . Apsara Ghritachi, who, on account of her energy, was then possessed of great beauty.

verses.sanskrit: स्वकर्माण्यभिसन्धाय नाभिनन्दति मे मनः । प्राप्य घोरं भयं नूनं मया वैवस्वतादपि ॥३॥
verses.english: Seeing the Apasara in those woods, the illustrious Rishi Vyasa, O Yudhisthira, became suddenly possessed by desire.

verses.sanskrit: तत्तु शल्यमनिर्हत्य कथं शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम् । सर्वं मन्युं विनीय त्वमभि मां वद शौनक ॥४॥
verses.english: The Apsara, seeing the Rishi's heart smitten with desire, changed herself into a she-parrot and came to that spot.

verses.sanskrit: महानासं ब्राह्मणानां भूयो वक्ष्यामि साम्प्रतम् । अस्तु शेषं कुलस्यास्य मा पराभूदिदं कुलम् ॥५॥
verses.english: Although he saw the Apsara disguised in another form, the desire that had arisen in the Rishi's heart spread itself over every part of his body.

verses.sanskrit: न हि नो ब्रह्मशप्तानां शेषं भवितुमर्हति । स्तुतीरलभमानानां संविदं वेदनिश्चितान् ॥६॥
verses.english: Inviting all his patience, the ascetic tried to suppress that desire. With all his efforts, however, Vyasa could not control his agitated mind. On account of the inevitability of what was to take place the Rishi's heart was drawn by Ghritachi's beauty.

verses.sanskrit: निर्विद्यमानः सुभृशं भूयो वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतम् । भूयश्चैवाभिरक्षन्तु निर्धनान् निर्जना इव ॥७॥
verses.english: He tried his best for making a fire for suppressing his emotion, but despite all his efforts his vital seed came out in the wood.

verses.sanskrit: न ह्ययज्ञा अमुं लोकं प्राप्नुवन्ति कथञ्चन । आपातान्प्रतितिष्ठन्ति पुलिन्दशबरा इव ॥८॥
verses.english: That best of twice-born ones, however O king, continued to rub his stick without feeling any scruples for what had taken place. From the seed that feil, was born a son to him called Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: अविज्ञायैव मे प्रज्ञा बालस्येव स पण्डितः । ब्रह्मन् पितेव पुत्रस्य प्रीतिमान् भव शौनक ॥९॥
verses.english: On account of this incident about his birth, he came to be called by the name of Shuka. : Indeed, it was thus that great ascetic, that foremost of Rishis and highest of Yogins, was born from the two sticks.

verses.sanskrit:
शौनक उवाच।
              
              किमाश्चर्यं ततः प्राज्ञो बहु कुर्यादसाम्प्रतम् । इति वै पण्डितो भूत्वा भूतानां नानुकुप्यते ॥१०॥
verses.english: As in a sacrifice a blazing fire spreads its effulgence all around when libations of clarified butter are poured upon it, similarly did Shuka take his birth, blazing with effulgence on account of his own energy.

verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञाप्रासादमारुह्य अशोच्यः शोचते जनान् । जगतीस्थानिवाद्रिस्थः प्रज्ञया प्रतिपत्स्यति ॥११॥
verses.english: Assuming the excellent form and hue of his father, Shuka, O son of Kuru, of purified Soul, shone like a smokeless fire.

verses.sanskrit: न चोपलभ्यते तेन न चाश्चर्याणि कुर्वते । निविण्णात्मा परोक्षो वा धिक्कृतः पूर्वसाधुषु ॥१२॥
verses.english: O king, coming to the breast of Meru, in her own embodied form, the foremost of rivers, viz., Ganga, bathed Shuka with her waters.

verses.sanskrit: विदितं भवतो वीर्यं माहात्म्यं वेद आगमे । कुरुष्वेह यथाशान्ति ब्रह्मा शरणमस्तु ते ॥१३॥
verses.english: There fell from the sky, O son of Kuru, an ascetic's stick and a dark deer skin for the use, O king, of the great Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: तद्वै पारत्रिकं तात ब्राह्मणानामकुप्यताम् । अथवा तप्यसे पापे धर्ममेवानुपश्य वै ॥१४॥

जनमेजय उवाच।
              अनुतप्ये च पापेन न च धर्मं विलोपये । बुभूषुं भजमानं च प्रीतिमान् भव शौनक ॥१५॥
verses.english: The Gandharvas sang repeatedly and the various clans of Apsaras danced; and celestial kettle drums of loud sound began to bcat.

verses.sanskrit:
शौनक उवाच।
              छित्त्वा दम्भं च मानं च प्रीतिमिच्छामि ते नृप । सर्वभूतहितं तिष्ठ धर्मं चैव प्रति स्मरन् ॥१६॥
verses.english: The Gandharvas Vishvavasu, and Tumvuru, and Narada, and those other Gandharvas called by the name of Haha, and Huhu, eulogised the birth of Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: न भयान्न च कार्पण्यान्न लोभात्त्वामुपाह्वये । तां मे दैवीं गिरं सत्यां शृणु त्वं ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥१७॥
सोऽहं न केनचिच्चार्थी त्वां च धर्मादुपाह्वये । क्रोशतां सर्वभूतानां हाहा धिगिति जल्पताम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: The Wind-god poured there showers of celestial flowers. The entire universe, mobile and immobile, became filled with joy.

verses.sanskrit: वक्ष्यन्ति मामधर्मज्ञं त्यक्ष्यन्ति सुहृदो जनाः । ता वाचः सुहृदः श्रुत्वा संज्वरिष्यन्ति मे भृशम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: The great and the highly effulgent Mahadeva, accompanied by the Goddess, and moved by affection, came there and soon after the birth of the Muni's son invested him with the sacred thread.

verses.sanskrit: केचिदेव महाप्राज्ञाः प्रतिज्ञास्यन्ति तत्त्वतः । जानीहि मत्कृतं तात ब्राह्मणान् प्रति भारत ॥२०॥
verses.english: Shakra, the king of the gods, gave him, from affection, a celestial pitcher of excellent form, and some celestial dresses.

verses.sanskrit: यथा ते मत्कृते क्षेमं लभन्ते ते तथा कुरु । प्रतिजानीहि चाद्रोहं ब्राह्मणानां नराधिप ॥२१॥

जनमेजय उवाच।
              नैव वाचा न मनसा पुनर्जातु न कर्मणा । द्रोग्धास्मि ब्राह्मणान्विप्र चरणावपि ते स्पृशे ॥२२॥
